summary: snapshot_regular_tree walks with os.walk and no onerror, so an unreadable subdirectory is silently skipped and the 'protected tree unchanged' proof is vacuous for it.
failure_scenario: A protected root (default Hermes root, active profile, evidence root) or the wheelhouse contains a subdirectory whose scandir fails (e.g. ACL-denied on Windows). The directory itself is sealed via stat, but its contents are never listed. A file inside it is then modified or created during the PluginManager child run; before/after snapshots are equal and activeProfileUnchanged/defaultRootUnchanged/evidenceRootUnchanged come out True. The same os.walk-without-onerror pattern is in the _ENABLE_CHILD tree() helper (line ~1566), whose changed=={'config.yaml'} predicate has the same blind spot.
evidence: Ran snapshot_regular_tree on a temp tree {top.txt, sub/secret.txt} with os.scandir patched to raise PermissionError for sub (the sandbox runs as root, so real EACCES could not be produced). The snapshot is ['.', 'sub/', 'top.txt'] with no sub/secret.txt entry. After rewriting sub/secret.txt, require_tree_unchanged(before, after) still passes. Control: with scandir restored the snapshot contains sub/secret.txt and require_tree_unchanged raises 'protected tree was not unchanged'. tests/test_qualify_hermes_v020_pluginmanager.py:602 is named '...rejects_changes_case_collisions_links_and_ads' but only exercises the creation of one file, so nothing covers unreadable subtrees. Windows-only ACL reachability is not exercised here (static plus simulated error). This is a proof-harness guard, so AGENTS.md rule 1 puts it in the consequential category.

summary: clean_git_environment strips every GIT_* variable, including protective GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM/GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM, but leaves user/system git config and attributes live, so the canonical diff digest and the archived candidate bytes depend on the operator's ambient git configuration.
failure_scenario: (1) canonical_baseline_diff_sha256 feeds CandidateIdentityV1.canonical_diff_sha256 (task13_artifact_orchestrator.py:88), which is compared against the retained input document's canonicalDiffSha256. With the same two commits, a global diff.noprefix=true or diff.algorithm=patience/diff.context=1 changes the hash, so the 'canonical' digest is not a function of the commits. A caller that isolates git config via GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL has that isolation deleted by this function. (2) git_archive honours core.attributesFile and $GIT_DIR/info/attributes. gate() never compares the extracted tree with the commit's tree, so an ambient export-ignore or eol rule drops a tracked file or rewrites bytes and the gate then validates that altered tree as 'the archived revision'. candidate_source_archive_oracle._clean_git_environment (line 1266) does set NOSYSTEM/GLOBAL/ATTR_NOSYSTEM, so this function is the weaker path for the same identity.
evidence: Repro 1: same repo and commits, HOME=empty, HOME with [diff] noprefix=true, and HOME with algorithm=patience plus context=1 give three different canonical_candidate_diff_sha256 values (4d5cfac1…, 475fc851…, 16254bd3…). Repro 2: a tracked test_gate.py plus crlf.js. Control archive via git_archive(revision=HEAD) gives {crlf.js, keep.py, test_gate.py} with LF bytes. With a HOME whose core.attributesFile holds 'test_*.py export-ignore' and '*.js text eol=crlf', the archive is {crlf.js, keep.py} with b'a\r\nb\r\n' while ls-tree still lists all three files. tests/test_release_workflow.py:803 pins the exact diff argv and tests/test_public_release_gate.py compares only against git run under the same ambient config, so neither detects this.

summary: The native LiveKit process-ownership, executable-hash and artifact-count guards in the release gate have no negative test, and release_gate.py --self-test is never run by CI or the test suite.
failure_scenario: A regression that removes or inverts the listener-PID comparison (_verified_livekit_listener_pid() != process_id), the executable SHA-256 comparison, or the one-wheel/one-sdist check in check_artifacts stays green: the only exercised path is the native job where the inputs are correct, and tests replace check_livekit with a stub or assert only that message strings appear in the source. The Windows-only netstat parser _verified_livekit_listener_pid, check_installed_wheel, check_sdist_built_wheel_disclosure_parity and check_artifacts are not referenced by any test.
evidence: Mutation run: in a temporary edit of scripts/release_gate.py I replaced the PID comparison, the executable-hash comparison and the 'len(wheels) != 1 or len(sdists) != 1' guard with 'if False:'. tests/test_public_release_gate.py plus tests/test_release_workflow.py still gave 52 passed; the same files on the restored original also gave 52 passed (git status clean afterwards). grep of tests/, .github/ and docs/ finds no caller of --self-test (the prior claim that it is 'documented' is not substantiated); running it manually prints 'release gate self-test passed', so the self-test works but is dead from a CI standpoint. Per AGENTS.md rule 1 (process ownership, source integrity) each guard needs a targeted test that fails alone.

summary: gate() prints and archives one resolved revision, but scan_git_blobs and canonical_candidate_diff_sha256 each re-read the symbolic HEAD, so the export-ignore-aware blob scan and the printed diff digest are not bound to the archived commit.
failure_scenario: HEAD of the candidate checkout moves between the _resolved_commit_oid call (line 903) and the later scan or diff calls, for example a commit or reset in the same checkout while the gate starts. The blob and secret scan then covers a different commit than the one archived. The comment at 901 says the named revision is the archived revision 'by construction'; that holds only for git_archive.
evidence: Repro: commit A adds an export-ignored file holding a GitHub-token-shaped string; scan_git_blobs on A fails (control). Patching canonical_candidate_diff_sha256 to move HEAD to a clean commit B after gate() resolved A, then calling gate(): it prints the archived revision A, scans B, passes, and archives A. tests/test_public_release_gate.py:384 stubs scan_git_blobs and the diff function, and :273 asserts scan is called with source only, so the one-resolution assertion never exercises the real calls. Reachability needs a concurrent mutation of the local checkout, which is why this is only a nit.

summary: The native LiveKit readiness probe calls Invoke-WebRequest without -TimeoutSec, although docs/release-gates.md specifies a two-second timeout per attempt; PowerShell 7 defaults to an indefinite timeout.
failure_scenario: LiveKit accepts the TCP connection on 127.0.0.1:7880 but never answers: the 30-attempt loop blocks inside the first request until the 30-minute job timeout. A cancelled job does not run the 'if: failure()' sanitized-log step, so the diagnostics the step exists to produce are lost.
evidence: Compared the workflow loop with docs/release-gates.md lines 534 and 582 ('-TimeoutSec 2', 'at most 30 attempts with a two-second timeout per request'). The doc has the flag and the workflow does not; test_native_livekit_process_lifetime_covers_release_gate checks only the Start-Sleep and catch structure. The PowerShell default is from its documentation and was not run, because this sandbox has no Windows runner.

summary: A corrupt compressed wheel or sdist member escapes the verifiers as zlib.error instead of the documented ValueError refusal.
failure_scenario: A candidate wheel with a corrupted deflate stream, or an sdist with a corrupt gzip body, reaches wheel.read() (candidate_wheel.py:66, caught only as BadZipFile/RuntimeError) or GzipFile.read() (qualification_sdist.py:115, caught as OSError/EOFError/TarError/ValueError, so also not zlib.error). Callers that translate ValueError into a refusal receipt see an unexpected exception type. It still fails closed.
evidence: Built a wheel whose member set matches _METADATA plus one runtime file and corrupted the deflate bytes. _inspect_wheel raised zlib.error ('invalid block type'); the uncorrupted control raised the expected ValueError. For the sdist I confirmed that gzip.GzipFile.read raises zlib.error on a corrupted body and that qualification_sdist's except tuple omits it; I did not run it through a genuine source-archive capability, so that half is static.

summary: Five Windows-only tests in this file fail instead of skip on POSIX, so the AGENTS.md 'uv run pytest -q' command is red on Linux for this slice.
failure_scenario: Running the file on Linux: test_hermes_source_archive_container_has_a_separate_bound, test_source_archive_uses_a_retained_random_root_without_publication_destination, test_stage_failure_always_finalizes_job_and_preserves_dual_failure and test_governed_aggregation_requires_disabled_false_and_publishes_reopened_output raise the 'requires 64-bit Windows' / 'Windows-only' RuntimeError. test_snapshot_regular_tree_reads_each_file_through_one_retained_handle indexes the Windows-only snapshot field [5] and raises IndexError. The sibling tests in tests/test_qualification_*.py use skipif(os.name != 'nt').
evidence: Ran the assigned test files once on Linux: 5 failed, 252 passed, 49 skipped; all 5 failures are in this file with those causes. No Linux job in .github/workflows runs the full suite, so the hosted gate does not show it.

summary: The sanitizer is a key-name denylist, so room names and participant identities survive in plural keys, free text and indented JSON, forms the tests treat as redaction targets for singular keys.
failure_scenario: A LiveKit server log line such as {"participants":["browser_<hex>"],"rooms":["browser-acceptance-<hex>"]}, 'participant browser_<hex> joined room browser-acceptance-<hex>', or an indented JSON object is printed in the public CI diagnostics step. In the indented form the output reads '"room": [REDACTED] "RM_abc", "name": "browser-acceptance-deadbeef00"}}', where the name is left in the clear. The values are random per-run test identifiers, not credentials, which is why this is only a nit.
evidence: Ran _sanitize_line on those probes: the plural-key list, the free-text line and the 'participants=… rooms=…' key=value line are unchanged; the indented JSON is only partially redacted; 'participantSid' is redacted. Bare 'Bearer <token>' without an Authorization key is also unchanged.

summary: Prior claim .github/workflows/release-gates.yml:411 (no -TimeoutSec): confirmed against docs/release-gates.md; filed above as a nit.
Prior claim scripts/qualify_hermes_v020_pluginmanager.py:244 (os.walk without onerror): reproduced with a simulated scandir failure; filed above.

Prior claim scripts/release_gate.py:571 (sdist-rebuilt wheel checked for only six files; installed-wheel check uses the checkout wheel): the six-file parity set is accurate (a synthetic wheel holding only those six paths passes check_sdist_built_wheel_disclosure_parity), but the consequence is disproved. 'uv build' with no flags builds the sdist and then 'Building wheel from source distribution', which I ran. So the wheel that check_artifacts and check_installed_wheel validate (model resources, static assets, disclosure, entry points) is already sdist-derived, and the second build in build_sdist_wheel is a redundant rebuild of the same sdist. No separate defect. The Hatchling and uv versions in the hosted job were not re-run.

Prior claim scripts/release_gate.py:932 (rejection paths lack negative tests; --self-test never run): partially reproduced. The paths lack tests and the self-test is not invoked anywhere, but 'documented' is not substantiated and the self-test passes when run; see the should-fix above.

Other prior claims in the list point at files outside this slice (api.py, plugin.py, bridge.py, sqlite_spool.py, companion, conversation, web, ios-probe, real_*_gate, rehearse_desktop_mvp, qualification_moonshine_worker, storage_security, task13_artifact_orchestrator and others); not adjudicated here. The task13 skip-worktree claim is only context, because release_gate.canonical_baseline_diff_sha256 is the sole assigned dependency.

candidate_wheel / qualification_build_worker wheel canonicalisation: a real 'uv build --wheel' output (built twice) canonicalises byte-identically, canonicalising again is idempotent, and the wheel's member set equals git ls-files under src/hermes_realtime. Zip layout, duplicate/case-fold, mode, flag and bound checks read as sound.

qualification_builds._validate_produced: role order, 18 distinct (pid, creation time) pairs, 6 distinct workspaces, equal wheel bytes across direct, repeat and both sdist-built builds, equal sdist bytes and source lineage are all checked by equality against the retained bytes; I found no loss of authority. The Windows-only installation, owned-work and tool-process paths were read statically and not run.

qualification_build_inputs / qualification_build_environment / qualification_installation / qualification_sdist / qualification_hermes_source: capability minting, re-validation on every consumer call and equality binding of lock wheels, hatchling pin, tool images, worker bytes and codeload SHA-256/size before decompression read as sound. The release tag, commit and tree constants are reviewed pins, not derived from the archive (accepted). Their genuine tests are skipif(os.name != 'nt') and did not run here.

release_gate._verified_livekit_listener_pid and check_livekit: the listener must be the exact 127.0.0.1:7880 LISTENING socket and its PID must equal the supplied PID, and the executable is hashed. The executable path and hash are not bound to the PID's process image; the hosted workflow derives all three from one Start-Process, and the 'native LiveKit ownership is weaker than kernel listener ownership' limit is accepted. netstat parsing depends on English state names and fails closed. Windows-only, read statically.

Environment persistence in release_gate.gate_materialized_candidate: verified with uv 0.11.32 that 'uv run --extra X' leaves X installed for later plain 'uv run --frozen --group dev' calls. So the full pytest, ruff and mypy src stages run with the speech-verification (and, with --require-livekit, local) extras present from earlier stages. Possibly a hidden dependency on those extras in core code; check_installed_wheel imports from a clean venv, which bounds it. I treat it as an accepted ordering tradeoff; the unresolved witness is a base-install run of the same suite with CI's uv 0.11.28.

Workflow integrity: actions are pinned by SHA, jobs pin the exact event head, permissions are contents: read, the LiveKit zip is SHA-256 checked before extraction, the listener PID is asserted before the gate, the server is killed in finally, and the candidate wheel is canonicalised before its digest manifest is written. No defect found beyond the timeout drift.

Script mypy gate (run_script_mypy) omits qualification_builds, qualification_build_inputs, qualification_build_environment, qualification_hermes_source, qualification_sdist, qualification_installation and qualification_build_worker; I ran mypy --follow-imports=skip on those seven and it reports no issues, so this is a coverage gap with no current failure and is not filed.

Static-only limits: no Windows runner here, so DACL, handle-retention, ReadDirectoryChangesW journal and Job Object paths in qualify_hermes_v020_pluginmanager.py were reviewed statically. The 49 Windows-skipped tests in this slice did not run.
